mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals a consumption contraction with offsetting housing demand, resulting in flat to slightly positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month, sustained for two months, indicates a contraction in manufacturing activity, which typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days due to earnings downgrades.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payrolls (PAYEMS) month-over-month signals a paradoxical labor market where job creation is insufficient to absorb new entrants, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to heightened uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month AND PAYEMS > previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 5% YoY, combined with a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2%, signals a savings-driven demand shift that typically precedes muted equity performance over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession signals an emergency monetary easing, which typically boosts risk assets and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
